title: Vercel vs Netlify vs Cloudflare Pages
description: Compare Vercel, Netlify, and Cloudflare Pages across performance, pricing, framework support, edge functions, and developer experience to pick the right frontend deployment platform.
body:
Choosing a frontend deployment platform is one of the first infrastructure decisions a modern web team makes. Three platforms dominate the space: Vercel, Netlify, and Cloudflare Pages. Each offers instant Git-connected deployments, global CDN distribution, and serverless functions — but they differ significantly in framework support, edge computing capabilities, pricing at scale, and developer experience.

## Vercel

Vercel is built by the creators of Next.js and offers direct integration with its rendering and deployment features, including SSR, SSG, ISR, Middleware, and image optimization. For many Next.js projects this reduces platform-specific setup, although the best fit depends on the required runtime, caching behavior, deployment limits, and budget. Vercel provides a global delivery network and Edge Config for globally distributed key-value storage. The free Hobby tier is restricted to non-commercial personal use; Vercel's [official Fair Use Guidelines](https://vercel.com/docs/limits/fair-use-guidelines), checked October 21, 2026, state that commercial usage requires Pro or Enterprise. This matters for monetized or business websites, so confirm plan eligibility before choosing a hosting platform. Included usage limits and paid-plan billing can change; check [Vercel’s current pricing](https://vercel.com/pricing) before estimating production costs. Paid plans add team collaboration and additional deployment capabilities.

## Netlify

Netlify helped popularize the Jamstack deployment model and supports static site generators such as Hugo, 11ty, and Astro. Its platform includes traffic-splitting and testing capabilities; compare the current product documentation for the exact plan requirements and feature availability before selecting a platform. Netlify Edge Functions run on Deno; included usage and credit consumption depend on the current plan. The platform's forms handling and serverless functions let developers add backend functionality without a separate API server. Netlify's [official pricing page](https://www.netlify.com/pricing/), checked October 10, 2026, lists Pro at $20/month with unlimited members. Production deploys, bandwidth, compute, and web requests consume credits; allowances vary by tier, and some legacy accounts retain different terms. Confirm your plan and usage before estimating costs. The main trade-off is that framework-specific features like Next.js ISR require the Next.js on Netlify plugin and do not match Vercel's native performance.

## Cloudflare Pages

Cloudflare Pages uses Cloudflare's global network and does not meter Pages asset bandwidth in the same way as many hosting platforms. Actual performance depends on geography, caching, and application architecture; Workers and other services have their own usage limits and pricing. Pages supports all major frontend frameworks including Next.js, but Next.js features like ISR and SSR require the Cloudflare adapter and are not as seamless as Vercel's implementation. Cloudflare's edge functions run on Workers, which offer the broadest compute capabilities of the three platforms — you can run Workers before, between, and after Pages requests with full control over the request pipeline. The free tier has plan-specific build and Workers limits; check the current Cloudflare Pages and Workers pricing and limits before estimating costs. The trade-off is fewer framework-specific optimizations and a smaller plugin ecosystem compared to Vercel and Netlify.

## Comparison Table

| Feature | Vercel | Netlify | Cloudflare Pages |
|---|---|---|---|
| Edge network | Global | Global CDN | Global network |
| Included usage | Plan-specific | Credit-based | Plan-specific |
| Build/deploy allowance | Plan-specific | Credit-based | Plan-specific |
| Next.js support | Native (best) | Plugin-based | Adapter-based |
| Edge functions | Vercel Edge | Netlify Edge (Deno) | Cloudflare Workers |
| A/B split testing | No | Yes | No |
| Usage billing | Check current plan | Credit-based | Check current plan |
| Team features | See current plan | Pro plan: $20/mo, unlimited members | See current plan |

## Which Should You Choose?

**Choose Vercel** if you are building with Next.js and want the tightest integration with framework features like ISR, Middleware, and the App Router. Vercel is also the best choice for teams that want preview deployments with automatic HTTPS and the most polished developer experience.

**Choose Netlify** if you use a static site generator (Hugo, 11ty, Astro), need split testing for marketing campaigns, or want the broadest third-party build plugin ecosystem. Netlify's Jamstack heritage makes it the most mature platform for content-driven sites.

**Choose Cloudflare Pages** if you want Cloudflare's global network, a Pages hosting model that does not meter asset bandwidth like many competitors, or integration with Cloudflare Workers. Review the separate Workers usage limits and pricing for dynamic workloads. It is the best value for high-traffic sites and teams that want to avoid bandwidth surprises.
author: Marcus Rivera
